children: ), a leading innovator in surgical treatments and therapies for atrial fibrillation (Afib), left atrial appendage (LAA) management, and post-operative pain management, today announced the completion of enrollment in the Box Lesion Creation with Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion to Reduce the Occurrence of New-Onset Atrial Fibrillation (BoxX-NoAF) clinical trial (NCT06989775). The trial enrolled 960 patients across participating centers worldwide and is designed to evaluate whether surgical ablation combined with LAA exclusion can reduce the occurrence of post-operative and longer-term atrial fibrillation in elevated-risk cardiac surgery patients.

The BoxX-NoAF trial is a foundational strategic initiative for AtriCure to expand the clinical and economic value proposition of its surgical ablation and LAA management technologies through high-quality randomized clinical evidence.

"Completing enrollment in BoxX-NoAF marks an important milestone and positions the trial as a meaningful upcoming catalyst," said Michael Carrel, President and Chief Executive Officer of AtriCure. "Together with LeAAPS, BoxX-NoAF advances our long-term clinical evidence strategy and reinforces AtriCure's leadership position in surgical therapies designed to improve outcomes for cardiac surgery patients. We believe successful outcomes will strengthen the evidence supporting our EnCompass and AtriClip platforms, creating additional growth opportunities through expanding treatment options for indicated cardiac surgery patients at risk of post-operative atrial fibrillation."

“Postoperative atrial fibrillation (POAF) is one of the most common and consequential complications after cardiac surgery,” said Richard Whitlock, MD, PhD, FRCSC, Cardiothoracic Surgeon, McMaster University, and Global Principal Investigator. “We believe that combining a box lesion with left atrial appendage (LAA) exclusion during surgery could meaningfully reduce the incidence of new-onset POAF and alleviate its many associated burdens, including stroke, longer hospital stays, and death. The BoxX-NoAF trial is yet another study that sets precedent regarding the execution of well-powered, methodologically robust studies to answer important questions in our field.”

Post-operative atrial fibrillation is among the most common complications following cardiac surgery and is associated with increased morbidity, longer hospital stays, higher healthcare costs, and greater risk of future atrial fibrillation. Despite its prevalence, no FDA-approved therapy currently exists specifically for the reduction of post-operative and longer-term clinical Afib in this patient population. BoxX-NoAF was designed to evaluate a potential approach to address this significant unmet need.

With enrollment complete, the study moves into its next phase, which includes ongoing patient follow-up, data collection, monitoring, and statistical analysis. Clinical data from participating sites are currently being aggregated and validated. AtriCure currently expects primary study results to be presented in mid-2027.
The company expects data from BoxX-NoAF, together with results from its broader portfolio of clinical programs, to further inform future treatment guidelines and regulatory submissions.

BoxX-NoAF is a prospective, multicenter, randomized clinical trial conducted under an FDA-approved investigational device exemption (IDE) evaluating the use of the AtriCure Isolator® Synergy™ EnCompass® Clamp together with the AtriClip® Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion System to reduce the occurrence of new-onset atrial fibrillation, including long-term atrial fibrillation, in elevated-risk cardiac surgery patients. The study enrolled 960 patients at participating centers worldwide. The use of these devices for this indication is investigational, and their safety and effectiveness for this use have not been established. For more information about BoxX-NoAF, https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT06989775

AtriCure, Inc. provides innovative technologies for the treatment of Afib and related conditions. Afib affects more than 59 million people worldwide. Surgeons around the globe use AtriCure technologies for the treatment of Afib, reduction of Afib-related complications, and post-operative pain management. AtriCure’s Isolator® Synergy™ Ablation System is the first medical device to receive FDA approval for the treatment of persistent and long-standing persistent Afib. AtriCure’s AtriClip® Left Atrial Appendage Exclusion System products are the most widely sold LAA management devices worldwide. AtriCure’s Hybrid AF™ Therapy is a minimally invasive procedure that provides a lasting solution for long-standing persistent Afib patients. AtriCure’s cryoICE cryoSPHERE® and cryoXT® probes are cleared for temporary ablation of peripheral nerves to block pain, providing pain relief in cardiac, thoracic and amputation procedures.
